palette.background: #f8f8f8 off-white, ~70% of frame at the final framing

content: Original: a small round-headed stick-figure villager (simple oval head, dot eyes, short brown hair tuft, leaf skirt, stick limbs) and a huge original creature: a brown furry ground-sloth-like beast with grey curved claws, drawn with hand shading.
timeline: f0: hard cut in. Villager alone, centred-left, LARGE: figure height ~75% of frame height. White background.

f13-15: a thin black vertical measurement bracket (|-shaped with short horizontal end ticks) and a 2-line small handwritten label (e.g. "4 ft 11 in (150 cm)" / "110 lbs (50 kg)") appear to the LEFT of the villager (simple pop-in, 1-3 frames).

f24-37 (14 frames): CAMERA ZOOM-OUT on the whole artwork: total scale factor ~0.43 (i.e. content shrinks to 43%), ease-in-out (slow-fast-slow, fastest around f30), plus a slight horizontal drift (~+120 px total). As it widens, the huge creature is revealed standing to the RIGHT, its height ~85% of frame; the villager + bracket + label are now small at lower-left.
f38-52: a second taller bracket + 2-line label (e.g. "13 ft 1 in (400 cm)" / "9,900 lbs (4,500 kg)") appears left of the creature, at upper-left of it.
f52-157: hold the composition (tiny idle allowed: e.g. 1-2 single-frame blink/pose swaps; no camera motion).

style.line: thick near-black (#080808..#202020) hand-drawn outlines, slightly uneven width 4-7px at 1080p; flat fills, at most a light hand-shaded texture; no gradients, no glow, no drop shadows
style.typography: handwritten / marker-style lowercase labels (font UNKNOWN in source; use any handwritten-looking font or draw strokes); never a geometric sans
style.originality: ALL characters, creatures, wording and objects must be NEW and original as specified here; do not imitate any existing show

deliverables: timeline.json: frame indices you used for every event
rules: You see only this spec. No source frames are provided or allowed. Use python3 + numpy + opencv (venv at ~/YIOS-local-audits/tooling/visual-ct-scan-venv/bin/python3) and ffmpeg (h264, yuv420p).
